description:
## Goal

Preserve exact partial composite returns across direct callable edges without falsely claiming that the whole tuple exists as a runtime ValueRef. A child field with a ValueRef representation is not evidence that its parent composite has a ValueRef carrier.

## Failure and cause

On behavior/mailbox_closure_reduce, the Enum.reduce wrapper lambda returns a semantic two-tuple under exact demand TupleFields([Ignore, Whole]). The :cont field is intentionally absent and the accumulator field is live. The transport recipe produces shape tuple(nothing, lane(any)) but lifts the live child carrier to the outer tuple. Backend and native then correctly interpret the outer ValueRef as a whole-materialization obligation and attempt to read the absent :cont value.

This is carrier provenance, not missing runtime demand. Do not widen the ignored tag, add a fallback Whole demand, or weaken backend/native validation.

## Correct model

Composite structural lanes and the optional whole-composite carrier are independent. Direct partial transport carries the demanded fields as multiple values with outer carrier Absent. ShapeDemand::Whole retains every structural lane; it does not itself request boxing. Only an explicit public, opaque, or first-class boundary attaches a complete composite ValueRef carrier, and that carrier requires every field needed for safe materialization. Joining inner field representations must not manufacture that parent obligation.

A carrier-bearing child has two inseparable facts: one physical ValueRef lane and the child's exact structural identity needed to materialize and interpret that lane. The existing tuple ShapeDescr stores only child ShapeIds. Replacing a carrier-bearing callable child with a bare typed lane erases its capture contract and makes native execution invalid; preserving only the structural ShapeId erases the child's ValueRef obligation. Transport layouts therefore form the recursive physical contract: ValueRef owns its typed LaneId, tuples contain child TransportLayouts, and callable captures contain TransportLayouts.

Elixir/OTP provides the guide: known-list Enum.reduce bypasses its tagged protocol wrapper and passes only the accumulator; generic Enumerable boundaries construct and pass a complete tagged tuple. Within local control flow, the Erlang Core optimizer replaces immediately destructured tuples with multiple values and reconstructs the composite only where a boxed term must cross or serve an opaque term boundary; Fz ShapeDemand::Whole can remain complete structural lanes on a direct path.

## Acceptance

1. Add a focused RED reproducing the exact wrapper return: TupleFields([Ignore, Whole]) yields tuple(nothing, live lane) with outer carrier Absent, and all three mailbox_closure_reduce doors pass.
2. Prove a live child ValueRef(LaneId) remains one child-local physical lane, retains its exact callable/composite structural contract, and does not promote its parent tuple carrier on a direct-only path.
3. Prove Whole direct consumers retain complete structural lanes with outer Absent, while explicit boxed/public/first-class carriers require complete safe materialization.
4. Preserve same-arity field reprojection and boxed-owner guarantees from fz-tfn.36.
5. Backend and native agree: neither reads an ignored field on a direct partial return, while both reject an actually incomplete whole-value materialization.
6. No widening, compatibility shim, aggregate authority, string identity, or new scan. Put carrier provenance at the data-model boundary that makes invalid states unrepresentable.
7. Run focused transport/runtime-demand/backend/native tests, mailbox fixture on all doors, full library, serial fixture matrix, formatting, check, strict clippy, and update agent/user docs where the carrier rule is described.
8. Ticket-scoped cold adversarial review before the single commit; close this ticket with that commit. Then resume fz-kdt.4.

## Data-model boundary

TransportCarrier::ValueRef(LaneId) names the typed physical value lane, making every TransportLayout self-contained. ShapeDescr::Tuple(Box<[TransportLayout]>) retains each child's structural descriptor and carrier recursively. CallableDescr.capture_layouts replaces the parallel capture_shapes and capture_lanes vectors, so callable construction consumes the same recursive contract and the width-zero greedy extra-lane workaround is deleted. ShapeDemand::Whole retains every resulting field layout and TupleFields retains its selected fields; neither structural demand manufactures an outer carrier. Public, opaque, and first-class recipe boundaries attach their explicit outer carrier separately, and the existing encoders require the composite value to be complete before satisfying it.

## Contract enforcement

Carrier provenance dominates structural interpretation at every encode/decode boundary: `ValueRef(lane)` consumes or emits exactly that typed lane, while `Absent` traverses the recursive structure. An outer-`Absent` tuple remains decomposed transport even when a child is boxed; field views decode each child layout later, without reconstructing the parent. A carrier lane carries a field only when its owned Ty covers that field under the same typed subtype rule as a structural lane.

One centralized physical-layout traversal preserves whether each leaf is structural or a carrier. Root and nested carrier lanes always publish `ValueRef` ABI/codegen representation from their owned `LaneId`; raw scalar representation is available only to structural leaves. Canonical rendering expands carrier lanes semantically rather than exposing mint-order ids.

Generic demand construction and same-arity tuple joins operate recursively on `TransportLayout`, so nested carriers are neither discarded nor promoted to their parent. Callable construction derives its descriptor, captures, and public boundary from one `capture_layouts` authority. Complete backend entry layouts, including carriers, participate in equality. Width is the allocation-free recursive sum of physical layouts; no generic-callable width fallback or duplicate structural walkers remain.

Focused proofs cover mixed structural/carrier children, boxed root tuples, carrier-vs-structural ABI representation for the same scalar Ty, canonical stability across opposite mint histories, nested generic construction and tuple joins, callable capture authority, and the `enum_reduce_suspend` allocation contract in addition to the mailbox and fz-tfn.36 reprojection fixtures.

## Cold-review corrections

`ShapeDemand::Whole` over an exact tuple type must recurse to complete child `TransportLayout`s; it must not fall through to one tuple-typed structural `Lane`. This keeps the direct path fully decomposed with outer carrier `Absent`. Non-tuple or non-exact tuple evidence may still use one structural value lane. Add a focused exact-tuple Whole test that would fail if generic construction mints a tuple-typed scalar lane.

`BoundaryDescr` stores `surface_arg_layouts`, preserving every argument root carrier. Callable-boundary seam lanes derive only from `BoundaryDescr.callable -> CallableDescr.capture_layouts` and `BoundaryDescr.surface_arg_layouts` through the centralized provenance-aware walker. Remove both flattened `published_capture_lanes` and `published_arg_lanes` fields, canon/test vocabulary, and construction plumbing. Structural scalar captures and arguments retain raw representation; carrier origins always force `ValueRef`. Prove a raw-capable carrier capture cannot be mislabeled `RawInt`, and that a carrier-bearing argument remains `ValueRef` while a structural argument of the same Ty remains raw.

Callable-boundary seam facts retain `shape: Some(physical.structural)` and identify each physical ABI occurrence with a monotonically increasing boundary slot over captures followed by surface arguments. The slot is derived from those authoritative layouts rather than stored as another lane array. This keeps repeated interned lanes and carrier/structural occurrences distinct without broadening provenance into unrelated seam kinds.
title: Keep direct partial tuple returns unboxed
